item.title: OMP Usage 0.2.0
item.description:
## OMP Usage Panel 0.2.0
### Highlights
- **Updates through GitHub (Sparkle 2.10.1).** Checks run roughly daily and are pull-based (no push); notifications are quiet and deferrable. Update Now / Skip This Version / Later / Turn Off Notifications, manual **Check for Updates…**, and an **Updates** settings tab. Automatic installation is off by default; automatic restarts wait until the app is idle. Feed and archive are authenticated with Ed25519 and a signed app-tree hash; a failed health check rolls back to the previous app. - **Unified Settings window.** One dark sidebar window with **Save & Apply** / **Cancel**, covering every user-editable field; compact provider selection, maximum and Left/Right placement live in **Display → Compact view**. - **Per-provider wings.** Choose which providers appear, a shared total maximum with one aggregate **More** control, and Left/Right placement for each provider. - **Reparent fix.** A ring no longer goes missing when a provider moves directly from the right wing to the left; already orphaned rings are repaired without resetting preferences. - **Dense metric cards.** Content-sized cards with smaller primary values, thin progress and inline footer, preserving zero, unknown, remaining-only, over-limit and estimated values. - **Custom dropdowns.** Provider/account pickers and Settings Providers/Labels/Metrics ID suggestions use custom scrollable lists with keyboard navigation, Escape-closes-list-only and outside-click dismissal.
### Upgrading
- Existing saved settings and policies are preserved: configuration, authentication, selected providers, per-provider placements, profile buckets, and check/notification/automatic-install choices. Saved compact preferences stay readable if an automatic rollback restores the previous version: provider membership, maximum and a default side are persisted in the older-compatible form, and per-provider Left/Right overrides are retained as extra data. The older UI cannot render mixed per-provider wings and uses the default side instead. Full compatibility of 0.2.0 settings with older versions is not promised. - Earlier `0.1.0` installs made from source before updater support cannot discover updates. They need one manual install of this release (source installer, below). An updater-enabled installation can discover newer releases through the signed feed; this release does not claim any future check has already run.
### Installation and trust
- The universal (arm64 + x86_64) ZIP is ad-hoc signed and authenticated with Ed25519, but it is **not** Apple Developer ID signed or notarized. A manually downloaded copy may be blocked or warned about by Gatekeeper. - The recommended path is the documented source installer (`npm run macos:install`), which also bootstraps updates. Do not bypass quarantine.

item.title: OMP Usage 0.2.1
item.description:
## OMP Usage Panel 0.2.1
### Multi-monitor stability - The default **System primary** display no longer depends on which monitor has focus, so the panel stops jumping between displays. - **Settings → Display → Panel placement → Monitor** (custom dropdown) can pin a connected physical monitor, identified by its display UUID. - If a pinned monitor is disconnected, the panel temporarily falls back to the System primary display, keeps your choice, and returns when the monitor reconnects. - The choice is staged with **Save & Apply** / **Cancel**. Changing placement only does not reset the collector or other configuration. - A manual anchor stays on the same monitor across ordinary refresh, clamping, rearranging and disconnect/reconnect, without clamped positions overwriting it. - Deliberately saving a different monitor clears the manual position override. **Reset position** also clears the override but keeps the monitor selection. - Existing manual position data is retained or migrated on upgrade and startup, not reset.
### Updates - Checks run roughly daily when enabled, not by immediate push; existing check, notification and automatic-installation choices are preserved. - Universal (arm64 + x86_64) ZIP, ad-hoc signed and Ed25519-authenticated; not Developer ID signed or notarized. - Source bootstrap is only needed for clients that do not yet have the updater.
### Testing note Verified on a real built-in Retina display plus a DELL U2417H for monitor selection, Cancel, Save, relaunch and focus-independent placement. Disconnect/reconnect is covered by a deterministic model regression; physical cable hotplug was not exercised.

item.title: OMP Usage 1.0.0
item.description:
# OMP Usage 1.0.0
- Distributed as a single DMG containing `OMP Usage.app` and a short `Install.txt`. - First launch opens a native setup window. It detects an existing Node.js 22.18+ and omp (including nvm), lets you edit or browse for their absolute paths, edit the omp profile (an existing default config is detected automatically), and installs on **Install & Open**. Clicking Install also registers a per-user login LaunchAgent. - The app copies itself without admin rights to `~/Applications/OMP Usage.app`, preserving quarantine and extended attributes, and relaunches from there. There is no `/Applications` link. - Node.js and omp are not bundled or installed; Setup does not read, copy or change omp credentials or plugins. An existing valid configuration is kept byte-identical; an invalid one is reported, not reset. - Existing users update through the in-app updater using the same feed, key and bundle identity; settings and preferences are preserved. - Not Developer ID signed or notarized (ad-hoc/Ed25519 signed). Gatekeeper may block the first downloaded copy before the app runs.
